## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Khallāṭiyapetivatthu* ("Dressed in Hair", Pv 10) is a verse text belonging to the *Petavatthu* collection [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. In this narrative, a female ghost (*petī*) explains the significance and efficacy of giving and sharing merit [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four translations across four languages for this text [SuttaCentral].

Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral link the text to two other stories in the *Petavatthu*: the *Dhanapālaseṭṭhipetavatthu* (Pv 19) and the *Nandakapetavatthu* (Pv 38) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analyses by DharmaNexus confirm these textual reuses, showing that segments §12.1–15.4 correspond closely with Pv 19 (§13.1–16.4) and segments §12.1–14.4 match Pv 38 (§36.1–38.4) identically [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial verse-sharing with the *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15) and *Nandāpetivatthu* (Pv 16), as well as extensive commentary coverage in both the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, related thematic or textual elements are referenced in several canonical and para-canonical works, including the *Bālapaṇḍita Sutta* (MN 129), *Devadūta Sutta* (MN 130 and AN 3.36), *Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 15), *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 20.3), and the *Saṅkiccajātaka* (Ja 530) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus also records a low-confidence algorithmic cross-language match with the Tibetan *Vinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus].
